author: WP17
summary: Short chapter framing free-direct and free-api as narrow sibling libraries beneath the 2D-only FREEDIRECT renderer: the dependency chain, 2D scope, pinning, why the layer distinction matters and a status matrix. Mostly current; corrected where stub methods report success, where free-direct is called pinned (nothing pins it) and by the missing CNA CI lane. The site had only ecosystem-level summaries; the new deep dive adds the chain, status-tag census, fopen containment and inherited limits.

concepts.text: free-direct is a separately versioned compatibility library for a deliberately narrow, game-driven DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectPlay-shaped surface, and free-api supplies selected Win32-shaped types and helpers beneath it; neither is the CNA framework and neither aims to emulate every Windows API.
tokens: neither Wine nor a general Win32 SDK

concepts.text: CNA's FREEDIRECT renderer adapts SpriteBatch, textures and render targets to free-direct's DirectDraw-shaped objects, using DirectDraw only and CNA's own SDL_Window passed as the HWND.
free-direct uses SDL3 internally, but that does not make FREEDIRECT part of the SDL_RENDERER family: it never calls SDL's 2D texture API, only DirectDraw-shaped COM calls.

Ownership and errors cross explicit boundaries in the chain GraphicsDevice/SpriteBatch -> FreeDirect adapter -> free-direct surfaces and presentation -> free-api host helpers; free-direct adds ../free-api itself when no free-api target exists and links it PUBLIC, while the free-eggbert and planetblupi games add free-api explicitly first.

target.evidence: free-direct@934f72ff:CMakeLists.txt (if(NOT TARGET free-api), target_link_libraries PUBLIC free-api::free-api); cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (FREEDIRECT block)

concepts.text: The graphics path is 2D: surfaces, Blt/BltFast, Lock/Unlock, palettes and colour keys where implemented, and presentation; CNA's renderer adds its own CPU compositor on top.
DirectSound-shaped audio and DirectPlay-shaped networking are sibling-library features, not part of CNA's graphics renderer; CNA keeps its own audio and networking.
tokens: DirectSound and DirectPlay stay out by design

concepts.text: Unsupported COM methods do not uniformly fail: QueryInterface stubs return DDERR_UNSUPPORTED, but IDirectDrawSurface::IsLost() always returns DD_OK and Restore() always succeeds, so surface loss is unobservable.
concepts.note: The unit says unsupported methods return the documented failure/null form; two STUBs report success.

concepts.text: Sibling behaviour is bounded to the revisions read (free-direct 934f72ff, free-api 53d7a312, both frozen since 2026-07-18); CNA pins neither, no CNA CI job builds FREEDIRECT, and a runtime result must name the CNA commit and both library commits.
tokens: names the CNA commit and both library commits

target.evidence: git log --all --since=2026-07-19 in both clones (empty); .github/workflows (no free-direct clone); modules/renderers/freedirect/examples/CMakeLists.txt

concepts.note: FreeDirect CTests register only with CNA_BUILD_TESTS, a non-Windows non-Emscripten host and FREEDIRECT selected; they use SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy.

concepts.text: An application that calls DirectDraw itself needs free-direct directly, while an XNA-shaped 2D game can select FREEDIRECT without ever seeing a COM interface.
The Blupi ports decide which layer owns each dependency from call-site evidence rather than presenting either library as a universal compatibility solution.
The CNA FREEDIRECT renderer is a current 2D-only public identity, declared Experimental, with capability answers qualified per feature.

free-direct is a narrow compatibility implementation pinned by no one (not 'separately pinned'), and free-api is a transitive host-support layer reaching CNA only through free-direct's PUBLIC link, not a renderer.
tokens: A transitive host layer beneath free-direct
